GBR-01

The interface is Vietnamese. Dates are dd/mm/yyyy, times are 24-hour HH:mm, and all times use the gym's time zone Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (UTC+7). Enumerated values are stored in English and displayed in Vietnamese.
All screens
Staff and members are Vietnamese; one time zone avoids off-by-one-day errors in expiry and attendance.
The system automatically on every screen and stored time
GBR-02

All amounts are whole Vietnamese dong. Catalogue prices already include VAT — exactly what the customer sees and pays. The VAT rate (P-10) is copied into each order, and the VAT amount is computed as price × VAT ÷ (100 + VAT), rounded to the dong. Screens show VAT as a breakdown, never as an extra charge.
All sales, payment and report screens
Customers pay exactly the listed price; VAT is shown for tax reporting without changing the price.
The system automatically on every price, order and report
GBR-03

The end date of every package, freeze, voucher and report period is the last valid day. A one-month package starting 05/09 ends on 05/10 and can be used for the whole of 05/10; the next package starts 06/10. If the target day does not exist in the target month (start 30/01 or 31/01), the last day of that month is used.
All dated records
Customers get the full last day they paid for; all modules count dates the same way.
The system automatically when computing end dates
GBR-04

Business limits are parameters P-01…P-23 stored in SystemConfigs. A change applies only to records created afterwards: each order keeps the VAT rate and payment deadline it was created with, and each subscription keeps the freeze allowance (P-01) and swap allowance (P-08) copied at sale. Values that are fixed in the system and not parameters: the 13:00 shift boundary (GBR-38), the 15-minute PT-sale hold (BR-93) and the 5-minute VNPay link validity (CBR-70).
All modules
The Manager can adjust business limits without a code change; existing orders stay as sold.
The system automatically, reading SystemConfigs when a record is created
GBR-05

No business record is physically deleted; "delete" switches it to Inactive (or Retired / Withdrawn), so history stays intact. The only physical deletions are: a Pending leave request withdrawn by its owner (BR-83), a body measurement deleted by the customer (BR-89), time slots that were created only for an expired or released PT-sale hold (BR-93), and the Exercise cache refreshed from wger (BR-92).
All entities
History, revenue and tax records must stay complete and traceable; the exceptions hold no financial or audit value.
The system automatically on every delete action
GBR-06

A record cannot be deactivated while another active record still refers to it. Exception: a catalogue package can be switched to "Stop selling" (Inactive) while customers still use it — running orders and subscriptions are unaffected (CBR-97).
All entities
Prevents orphan or broken references (e.g. a PT with future sessions) without blocking the catalogue.
The system automatically before every deactivation
GBR-07

Every sensitive action — price or catalogue change, account action, contact or password change, deletion, approval or rejection, cancellation, session handling, shift action and every background-job state change — is written to the audit log in the same transaction as the change.
All modules
Lets the Admin trace who changed money, accounts and decisions.
The system automatically on every sensitive action
GBR-08

Each audit line reads as a plain sentence: who – in which role – did what – to what – from which value to which value – when – why. Background-job lines have no account and no role. Passwords and verification codes are never written. Only the Admin can read the log.
Audit log
The Admin can read the log without technical knowledge.
The system automatically when writing the audit log
GBR-09

Every negative or corrective staff action — rejecting a request, cancelling a session or order, deleting a profile, voiding, a cash variance, approving a leave request after it started (BR-86) — requires a written reason of 5–500 characters, stored with the record and in the audit log. Customers are never asked for a reason.
All approval and cancellation actions
Negative decisions must be explainable to customers and staff.
The system on submit (reason required, 5–500 characters)
GBR-10

Each action can be performed only by the role the user is working in (Guest, Customer, PT, Receptionist, Manager, Admin) according to the permission matrix; users see and change only the data their role allows. A user who holds several roles chooses one after signing in (CBR-113).
All screens
Each role sees and does only what its job requires.
The system on every page and request (role filter per URL area)
GBR-11

PT slots, single-session bookings and check-ins must fall within the opening hours of that day (P-19 or the date's exception). PT package sessions are generated on every chosen weekday of the term, including closed days, and must then be rescheduled by the PT (CBR-56).
Scheduling, booking, check-in
Nothing can be booked or used while the gym is closed.
The system automatically on every time-based action
GBR-12
Everyone who uses a service — members, dependants and walk-ins — has exactly one active customer profile.
All customer-facing features
Avoids duplicate members and split purchase history.
The system on profile creation (phone/email duplicate check)
GBR-13

Every rule checked on a screen is checked again on the server; the server never trusts values sent by the interface (identity, prices, ids). Competing actions on the same record are resolved by locks and conditional updates in one transaction — the later request is refused with a reload message.
All modules
Values sent from the browser can be altered.
The system on the server for every request
GBR-14

Time-based rules run without user action. Daily at 00:05 (UTC+7), in order: JOB-01 freeze resume, JOB-02 package expiry, JOB-03 day-pass expiry, JOB-04 PT session auto-close, JOB-08 gym-access reminder. Every minute: JOB-05 overdue online orders, JOB-06 timed-out transactions, JOB-07 leave reminder. A daily job that fails on a database error is retried every 5 minutes. Expired PT-sale holds are released when the PT-sale screen is next used (BR-93).
All time-based states

Background job scheduler
GBR-15

Notifications, sign-up, recovery, counter account
Email is free and reliable; SMS is out of scope.
The system when sending codes and notifications
GBR-16

Sales, payment, reports
Keeps the project scope; accounting is done in the gym's existing tools.
Business process (outside the system)
GBR-17

Required fields are marked *. Validation runs when leaving a field and again on submit; each error appears in red under its field. An error returned by the server is shown when the page opens and disappears as soon as the user corrects the field.

GBR-37

All screens

GBR-38

Each day is split into two shifts at 13:00: the morning shift runs from the opening time of the day (default 05:30, P-19) to 13:00 and the afternoon shift from 13:00 to the closing time (default 22:00). A slot, session or leave belongs to a shift by its start time (before 13:00 = morning). The same boundary is used by leave requests, the CBR-83 check, PT slot locking during leave, PT-sale shift assignment, the PT schedule divider and Receptionist shifts.
Leave, PT schedule, PT sale, shifts
One boundary everywhere avoids a session counted in two shifts.
The system (one shared constant)
GBR-39

The account badge on every screen shows the full name, initials avatar (or uploaded avatar) and a role code: KH-nnnn Hội viên, PT-nnnn Huấn luyện viên, LT-nnnn Lễ tân, QL-nnnn Quản lý, QT-nnnn Quản trị viên. Only the prefix changes for display; the stored codes stay KH-nnnn / NV-nnnn (DBR-09).
All signed-in screens
Users always see which role they are working in.
The system on every signed-in page
CBR: A New customer becomes Active as soon as their first membership package or day pass is paid. Paying for a PT package does not change the member state.
An Expired member becomes Active again as soon as a new membership package or day pass is paid. Paying for a PT package does not change the member state.
When the membership package reaches its end date, an Active member becomes Expired.
Nobody may edit an Inactive profile. The Receptionist cannot see it, the Manager sees it read-only, and the Admin traces its history through the audit log.
A New customer may buy a first membership package or day pass, but not a PT package (CBR-59).
An Expired member may buy a new membership package or day pass to continue; buying a PT package requires a valid membership package first (CBR-59).
The maximum number of freezes per package is configured by the Manager (P-01, default 1) and copied into the subscription at sale.
The maximum freeze duration is configured by the Manager (P-02, default 1 month).
Changing a package price or description in the catalogue never applies retroactively to existing orders.
The price of an existing order cannot be edited. A wrong order is cancelled and a new one is created.
The Receptionist may cancel a Paid counter order only within the shift that created it and before the shift is closed; the money is returned to the customer at the counter.
Every price belongs to a specific package in the catalogue; there are no free-standing prices.
Customers younger than P-05 (default 10 years) cannot buy a single PT package.
Customers younger than P-05 (default 10 years) cannot buy or join a couple PT package.
Customers younger than P-05 (default 10 years) cannot book a single PT session.
A member who still has a running package or unused PT sessions goes to Pending deletion and waits for Manager approval.

A customer profile and a login account are separate records. Every Self profile created online or at the counter gets its login account at the same time (CBR-24, CBR-31); only Dependent profiles are created without an account. A Self profile that has no account is activated by the customer online through UC-Claim (CBR-20, CBR-25, CBR-27).

A login account is required for every Self profile and is never created for a Dependent profile (CBR-21). A Self profile gets its email and account when it is created, whatever package it buys (including day passes).

If the Receptionist enters, in the customer profile form, a phone number that matches an active Person, the system opens that Person's customer profile. If the Person has no customer profile that is not Inactive (for example an employee), the Receptionist checks an identity document and creates the customer profile on the same Person instead of a new Person (CBR-114). On the quick-create form of the sales screen a matching phone number is refused instead (CBR-118).

If a guest signs up with the phone number of an active self-owned profile that has no account and enters the same email as the profile, the system sends a verification code to that email instead of creating a new profile; after the correct code and a password, the account is attached to the existing profile.
A Dependent profile has no login account.
The guardian only needs to be present at registration, not at every session.
If a phone number matches no active Person (only Inactive ones), a new Person and profile are created normally.

When the Receptionist creates a Self profile — on the quick-create form of the sales screen or in the customer profile form — the login account is created in the same transaction with the Person's email and a temporary password (CBR-31), whatever package is bought. If the Person already has an account (for example an employee, CBR-19), no second account is created: the existing account now also serves the Customer role (DBR-65).

A guest signing up with the phone number of a self-owned profile that has no account, but with a different email from the one on the profile, cannot activate it. The system says the phone number is registered with another email (masked); the guest uses that email or asks the Receptionist to verify and update it.

If a guest signs up with the phone number of an active Person that already has a login account, no account or profile is created; the system says the number already has an account and points to Sign In / Forgot Password, without saying whose number it is. An employee who also wants to train as a customer gets the customer profile at the counter (CBR-19), never through online sign-up.
A self-owned profile without an email cannot be activated online; the customer goes to the counter so the Receptionist can add the email, which creates the account (CBR-24).

Duplicate checks during self sign-up only compare against the phone number on Person; guardian numbers recorded on Dependent profiles neither block nor activate anything — the guardian registers as a new customer.

When the email of an account changes, by the account holder (UC-04) or by the Receptionist (UC-16), the system sends a warning to the old email and signs out every session of that account except the one that made the change. The email is stored on Person, so the change applies to every role of that Person.

In their own account a customer can change only the avatar (upload or remove), email, phone number and password. Full name, date of birth, check-in photo and guardian details are changed by the Receptionist (UC-16), because they are used for check-in verification and the PT age rule. Email and phone number changes follow CBR-110.

An account created by the Receptionist (CBR-24) is Active immediately and gets a random temporary password of 10 characters containing at least one letter and one digit, without look-alike characters (0, O, o, 1, l, I); only its BCrypt hash is stored. The system emails the temporary password together with the customer code before the transaction commits; if the email cannot be sent (or takes longer than 10 seconds) nothing is saved — neither the profile nor the account — and MSG04 is shown. The Receptionist sees the masked email in the success toast (MSG122). The customer signs in with email or phone number and the temporary password and may change it later in Account Settings; a change is not forced. The Sign In screen explains this in a hint box. A Dependent profile gets no account and no email (CBR-21).

A Dependent profile has no self-service channel: it cannot view schedules, book single sessions, reschedule or cancel PT sessions itself. Packages and single sessions are bought at the counter (UC-20, UC-21, CBR-54); PT sessions are rescheduled by the PT at the guardian's request through session handling (BR-64); schedules are checked with the Receptionist or the PT. Cancellation is not supported — an absent customer's session becomes Missed (CBR-42).

Before acting at the counter on behalf of a Dependent profile, the Receptionist verifies the requester with one of the guardian phone numbers recorded on the profile (DBR-25) or the customer code. The PT agrees changes with the customer or guardian outside the system before handling a session (BR-63); the system does not ask the PT to verify a phone number.
A paid day pass is valid immediately.
A check-in photo is mandatory for every package except the day pass; the Receptionist takes it at the counter when the customer first buys a package, or at the first check-in (BR-33).
A day pass gives exactly one entry to the gym.
The avatar uploaded by the customer is for display only and is never used for check-in verification.
The check-in photo belongs to the customer profile, not to the account. Only the Receptionist can take or retake it; the customer cannot change or delete it, even with an account.

When booking a single session online, customers can only choose slots in the current week (today to Sunday); from Saturday, slots of the following week also become available. The Receptionist scheduling a PT package and a PT rescheduling or transferring a session are not bound by this limit.

The hold of an online single-session slot lasts exactly as long as the order's payment deadline (P-09, copied into the order at creation — GBR-04); there is no separate slot timer. A Failed or Expired transaction does not release the slot: the order is still Pending, so the slot stays Held and the customer can pay again within the deadline (CBR-69).

A customer can hold slots for only one Pending single-session order at a time. Creating a new single-session order while an older one is Pending cancels the older order (type: replaced by a new order — CBR-71) and returns its slot to Free.

The PT does not mark attendance. After the session day has ended, JOB-04 (daily 00:05) closes every session still Scheduled: a session on a date declared closed all day → Cancelled / GymClosed (CBR-56); otherwise, if nobody in the session can use the gym that day (CBR-117) and someone is frozen → Missed / MembershipFrozen; if nobody can use the gym and nobody is frozen → Missed / NoMembership; otherwise, if the customer (couple: either member) checked in that day → CheckedIn; otherwise → Missed / NoCheckIn. Each session is closed in its own transaction with an audit line; the slot and commission are not changed. CheckedIn only means the customer entered the gym that day, not that the PT session was confirmed.

A PT package schedule is built from a weekly template: for each weekday Monday–Friday the Receptionist chooses either no session or one start time (1–5 sessions per week), on the chosen PT's slots. Individual dates can be overridden with another time or no session (BR-41). The most frequent start time is stored as the package's fixed start time. Sessions moved later by the PT keep their own time (BR-64, BR-65).
Withdrawn — customers do not swap sessions. The PT moves sessions only to slots they have published (BR-64).
Withdrawn — customers do not swap sessions. A PT rescheduling or transferring a session (BR-64, BR-65) is not restricted to weekdays.

After a reschedule, transfer or cancellation by the PT, the system immediately sends a bell notification to the customer (couple: both members) whose account is Active, and on a transfer also to the receiving PT. Dependent profiles are informed outside the system.
The system does not handle the case where one member of a couple package drops out.
PT packages (single and couple) are not sold online; they are sold at the counter only. Screens that suggest renewing a PT package point the customer to the counter (hotline and opening hours).

Single and couple PT packages are paid at the counter in cash or by bank transfer only. A single session booked online is paid through the online gateway (CBR-53); a single session bought at the counter is paid in cash or by transfer (CBR-54).

When a PT package order is Paid, the system creates one Scheduled session for each held date in the same transaction: the held slots become Booked and each session stores its session value and commission (DBR-58, DBR-59).
The customer cannot change PT midway when the PT is not at fault.

PT package times are chosen from the PT's published slots. If a chosen time is a slot the PT has not opened on that date, the Receptionist must tick "Confirmed with PT" before holding; the system then creates that slot as part of the hold (BR-96).

Booking a single session: choose a PT → choose a time from the PT's published schedule → the system creates a Pending order and holds the slot immediately (Held — DBR-36) → the customer pays within the order deadline → when the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked and the session is created. If the deadline passes unpaid, the slot returns to Free.

Selling a single session at the counter: when the customer confirms, the system creates a Pending order and the slot becomes Held immediately for the order's payment deadline (P-09, default 20 minutes, shown as an mm:ss countdown — GBR-27). When the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked and the session is created; if the deadline passes unpaid, the order is Cancelled and the slot returns to Free. A Failed or Expired transaction keeps the slot Held while the order is still within its deadline (CBR-40, CBR-69).

When a PT package passes its end date, the subscription becomes Expired automatically. Any Scheduled session left in the package (after reschedules or transfers) becomes Cancelled at the same time (PackageExpired), with no refund and no term extension.

Sessions are still generated on a date declared closed (the PT sale screen marks them). Before that date the PT must reschedule them (BR-64, no swap quota used); the PT dashboard lists them and JOB-08 does not remind customers for that day. A session still Scheduled after the closed day is cancelled by JOB-04 as GymClosed: no commission, no make-up, no term extension.
Withdrawn — merged into CBR-56: a closed day declared after the order is Paid is handled exactly like any other closed day (sessions stay Scheduled for the PT to reschedule).
A PT package or a single session only pays for the trainer; it does not include gym access. Gym access comes only from a membership package or a day pass.

A PT package order (single or couple) can be created only for a customer who holds a membership package valid today and is not frozen — a day pass does not count. Otherwise the Receptionist sells a membership package first (UC-20); only after it is Paid is the PT package order created. A Receptionist cannot sell to their own customer profile, and an employee who also trains as a customer must choose a different PT (CBR-115).

A single session can be booked only on a date covered by a valid membership package, or for today if the customer holds a valid day pass (CBR-34, BR-32). A walk-in who wants a single PT session buys today's day pass, then the Receptionist sells today's session at the counter (CBR-54).

When the PT reschedules a session (UC-35), a target date on which the customer cannot use the gym (CBR-117) is allowed but highlighted in amber; the session then shows "needs attention" and JOB-08 reminds the customer the day before.

A freeze is never blocked by PT sessions and does not change them when it is saved: future sessions inside the freeze period stay Scheduled and are shown with the warning "inside the freeze period" on the customer's and PT's screens. After each session day JOB-04 closes such a session as Missed / MembershipFrozen when nobody in the session could use the gym (CBR-42). The freeze applies only to the membership (BR-21), so the PT package term does not move. Before saving, the system lists the sessions that fall inside the freeze period so the Receptionist can inform the customer.

A valid day pass counts as gym access for that day, also for PT package sessions (CBR-117). A customer with remaining PT sessions but no valid membership must buy a membership package or a day pass for each session day; otherwise JOB-04 closes the session as Missed / NoMembership.

A PT package session on a day when nobody in it can use the gym (CBR-117) is closed by JOB-04 as Missed / NoMembership (or MembershipFrozen). It is deducted like a no-show (BR-52) and still earns commission (CBR-80). The system neither reschedules the session nor extends the PT package; the customer is reminded the day before (JOB-08).

The membership does not have to cover the whole PT term: a PT package can be sold as soon as the customer (couple: each member) holds a membership valid today (CBR-59). The customer search on the PT sale screen shows each customer's membership end date ("gym package until dd/mm") so the Receptionist can suggest a renewal; sessions that later fall on days without gym access are labelled (CBR-66) and reminded by JOB-08. A PT package still never grants gym access (CBR-58).

A Scheduled session on a day the customer cannot use the gym (CBR-117) is labelled on the customer's schedule ("no gym package" / "inside freeze period" / "gym closed") and in the PT dashboard "Needs attention" block. The label disappears when a membership or day pass covering that day is bought.

A couple-package session is closed as Missed for lack of gym access only when both members cannot use the gym that day; if one member is frozen and the other can use the gym, the session follows the normal check-in rule (CBR-42).

Sessions closed as Missed / MembershipFrozen earn commission like any Missed session (CBR-80); their past slots are not released. Missed is final (DBR-38). If the freeze is cancelled early, sessions after the actual end date simply stay Scheduled.
When a transaction becomes Failed or Expired the order stays Pending; the customer can pay again for the same order while it is within its deadline.

An online Pending order with no Success transaction by its payment deadline (P-09, default 20 minutes) becomes Cancelled (type: payment deadline passed), and its Pending transaction becomes Expired. Each VNPay payment link is valid for 5 minutes but never beyond the order deadline. Paying after the deadline is refused (MSG146). To buy again the customer creates a new order; price and voucher are re-evaluated.
When a customer creates a new online order for the same package while an older online order for it is Pending, the older order becomes Cancelled (type: replaced by a new order).

If the gateway reports success but the order is already Cancelled or the amount does not match exactly, the transaction is still recorded as Success, the order is not Paid (if not yet cancelled it becomes Cancelled, type: invalid payment), no entitlement is created, and the transaction goes to the Manager's refund list (BR-81).

A voucher is valid when all of these hold: it is Active, within its validity period, total uses remain, the customer has not exceeded their allowed uses (CBR-74), the order's package type is within the voucher scope (CBR-76), and the package price before discount reaches the minimum order value.

Each customer may use a voucher at most the number of times configured on it (default 1; empty = unlimited). Uses are counted on orders held by the customer that are not Cancelled, including Pending ones.
A voucher cannot be added, removed or changed while the order has a Pending transaction.

Each voucher has a scope chosen by the Manager: membership packages & day passes (default) or membership packages only. PT packages and single sessions never accept a voucher; the PT sale screen has no voucher field.

The Receptionist confirms a bank transfer at the counter only after checking that the money has arrived in the gym's account (tick "received in full"; optional transfer reference up to 50 characters).
The Receptionist can close a shift only when no counter order created in that shift is still Pending: each must be paid or cancelled (type: cancelled by the Receptionist) first.
The cost of goods is outside the system's scope.
A Missed session earns the PT commission like a CheckedIn one, because the customer's absence is not the PT's fault.
A session cancelled by the PT under BR-66 earns commission like a CheckedIn one, because the PT has repaid the customer in cash.
Withdrawn — customers do not cancel sessions (UC-39 withdrawn). Historical sessions cancelled ByCustomer keep their stored commission in reports.

A PT cannot submit a leave request for a shift (GBR-38) in which they still have a Scheduled session; the form lists the blocking sessions with a link to session handling on the PT schedule. While a leave request is Pending or Approved, the PT's free slots in that shift are locked (shown "leave pending" / "leave approved"), cannot be booked by a PT sale, cannot be used as reschedule or transfer targets, and the PT cannot publish new slots there. A booked session is never hidden by a leave request.

A leave request must be submitted before the submission cut-off on the day before the leave (P-12, default 15:00). After the cut-off the system refuses it (MSG192) and the employee informs the Manager directly. Example: leave on Thursday → deadline 15:00 Wednesday.

There is no approval deadline and no automatic rejection. A Pending request whose leave starts today or tomorrow is flagged "leave soon" and listed first; JOB-07 sends the Manager one bell reminder for the Pending requests starting tomorrow. A request whose leave has already started can still be approved under BR-86.

When a role of a Person becomes Inactive — the employee resigns (UC-13) or the customer profile is deleted (UC-16, UC-17) — every session of that Person's account is signed out immediately. If the Person still has another role that is not Inactive, the account stays Active and from then on serves only that role; otherwise the account becomes Inactive, which is final (DBR-28).

An employee's position can change only when no unfinished work remains in the old position: a PT has no Scheduled session, no future slot and no running PT package; a Receptionist has no open shift. Changes to or from Admin follow BR-08.
Each shift must keep at least P-13 (default 2) PTs on duty after leave is approved.
The Receptionist also looks after the gym facilities: they view the catalogue, report broken equipment and close repaired requests.
Each shift must keep at least P-14 (default 1) Receptionist on duty after leave is approved.
A PT can edit only the private notes and workout/meal plans they created; everyone can edit only their own account profile.
A private note about a customer is visible only to the PT who wrote it — even after the customer moves to another PT, the new PT cannot see it.

After a successful password change in Account Settings (UC-04), every other session of that account is signed out; after a password reset through Forgot Password (UC-03), every session is signed out and a temporary sign-in lock is cleared.

A verification or recovery code allows P-17 (default 5) wrong entries. On the last wrong entry the code is cancelled and verification for that email is locked for P-18 (default 5) minutes — no entry and no new code during the lock. Requesting a new code is allowed 60 seconds after the previous one; the 5th request within an hour triggers the same lock. A new code always cancels the previous one.

Staff accounts (Admin, Manager, PT, Receptionist) are created only by the Admin. If the phone number matches an active Person (for example a customer), the staff role is attached to that Person instead of a new Person (CBR-114); if that Person already has an account, no second account is created — the existing account now also serves the staff role (DBR-65). Customer accounts come from exactly two sources: online self sign-up (UC-05) or creation by the Receptionist at the counter (CBR-24). The Admin never creates customer accounts.
An account is blocked from signing in only in three cases: it is Inactive because every role of its Person is Inactive (CBR-86), the Admin has locked it, or it is temporarily locked under BR-01.
An Inactive (stopped) package is no longer sold online or at the counter; running orders and subscriptions of that package are unaffected and still appear on the customer's screens.
A voucher used at least once can only be deactivated, never deleted.

Equipment is never hard-deleted, and management works at two levels: a facility group can only be hidden or shown in the Receptionist catalogue (IsActive), and an individual equipment item is retired (Retired). An item that still has an Open or In Progress maintenance request cannot be retired. A retired item is excluded from quantities and can no longer be reported broken.
A blog post switched to Inactive disappears from the public site immediately.

When the Manager approves a maintenance request, the individual equipment item of that request (not the whole facility group) switches to UnderMaintenance automatically, unless the Manager unticks "Set item to Under maintenance" because the item can still be used while waiting for the repair.
When the Receptionist closes a maintenance request, the equipment item returns to Available automatically only if it has no other request still In Progress and it has not been Retired.
The audit log and audit-related metrics are visible to the Admin only; the Manager's report does not include them.
Each open day has exactly two duty shifts — morning (opening–13:00) and afternoon (13:00–closing), GBR-38 — derived from the opening hours; there is no manual rostering.

The Receptionist on duty opens the shift at its start and closes it at its end; every payment taken while the shift is open is recorded in that shift. Counter sales and counter payments are refused while no shift is open (MSG109, MSG110).
Only the Manager can read customer feedback; PTs and Receptionists cannot. A PT sees only their own monthly average rating (DBR-69).

Each piece of feedback has a submission time and a read/unread state. There is no reply or resolution workflow — the Manager only reads it. Re-rating the same PT in the same month makes the feedback unread again (DBR-67).

In their own account a staff member can change only the avatar, email, phone number and password. Personnel details are view-only: full name, date of birth, employee code, position, hire date and employment status for every staff role; a PT also sees specialty, years of experience and commission rate. These details are changed by the Manager (UC-13); position and account status only by the Admin (CBR-109); the employee code never changes (DBR-09). Full name and date of birth are stored once on Person: whether changed by the Manager (UC-13) or the Receptionist (UC-16), the change applies to every role of that Person and is logged (CBR-112). Email and phone number changes follow CBR-110.

Role, position and account status (active / locked) are never editable in Account Settings. Only the Admin changes an employee's position (UC-07, CBR-87, BR-08) and locks or unlocks an account. A role is added by creating a customer profile (CBR-19, CBR-24) or a staff role (CBR-95) on the Person, never by editing the account. The only automatic changes are CBR-86 and the temporary lock of BR-01.

Changing the email or phone number in Account Settings (UC-04), in any role, requires a 6-digit verification code: for a new email the code is sent to the new email; for a new phone number it is sent to the account's current email. The new value must differ from the current one and is checked for duplicates (DBR-22, DBR-23) before the code is sent and again when it is saved; the value saved is exactly the one the code was issued for (GBR-13). The user may cancel a pending change. Email and phone number are stored on Person, so the change applies to every role. Changes made at the counter by the Receptionist (BR-19) need no code.

The Dependent profiles tab of Account Settings is shown only when the user is working in the Customer role (CBR-113); it lists, read-only, the Dependent profiles whose guardian phone is the account's phone number, with whether each can use PT services (P-05). A staff role never sees it.

Changes of email, phone number, avatar and password in Account Settings, and changes of the personal data stored on Person by the Manager or the Receptionist, are written to the audit log as readable sentences (GBR-08) that state the role the user was working in. Passwords and verification codes are never written to the log (DBR-02). If the change is saved but the audit line fails, the user is told (MSG302).

A user signs in with email or phone number and password; either one identifies exactly one account (DBR-22, DBR-23, DBR-65). If the account serves more than one role that is not Inactive, the system shows the role selection screen — the staff position or Customer — before opening any home screen. The session holds exactly one role, and every screen and permission follows that role (GBR-10). The user can switch role at any time from the account menu without signing in again; an account with a single role goes straight to that role's home screen.

The phone number identifies the Person. When a customer profile or a staff role is created for a phone number that matches an active Person who does not hold that kind of role (DBR-65), the Receptionist or the Admin checks an identity document and attaches the new role to that Person: no second Person is created, and full name and date of birth are taken from the Person. This happens only in the customer profile form (CBR-19) and in staff account creation (CBR-95); online sign-up never attaches a role to an existing Person (CBR-26) and directs such a phone number to the counter.

A Person must not act in a staff role on their own customer profile: when the signed-in staff role and the customer profile belong to the same Person, the system blocks selling or changing a package, applying a voucher, freezing, editing or deleting the profile, approving its deletion, refunding, and any PT sale, session handling, note or plan in which the same Person is both trainee and PT. Another employee with the required permission performs the action instead.
A customer may rate a PT for a month only if, in that month, they (or their couple partner on the same package) have at least one session with that PT closed as CheckedIn or Missed.

"Can use the gym" on a date means: the customer holds a Membership or a DayPass that covers that date and is not frozen on that date. A couple-package session is blocked only when neither member can use the gym. This single definition is used by JOB-04, JOB-08, the customer schedule and bookings, the customer dashboard and the PT dashboard.

Quick-create customer on the sales screen (UC-20): Self profile — full name (DBR-01), date of birth (DBR-04), phone number (DBR-17) not used by any existing customer, and email (format and DBR-23) are required; the account is created under CBR-24 / CBR-31. Dependent profile — full name, date of birth, guardian name (2–50 characters), relationship (required, up to 30 characters) and guardian phone are required; no email and no account. The profile starts as New with a new customer code.

Start dates of membership packages and day passes: a day pass always starts on the day it is paid (CBR-34). A membership package starts the day after the customer's current membership ends if that membership has not expired (chained, not selectable); otherwise it starts today, or — at the counter — on a date chosen up to 7 days ahead. After an online purchase the customer may move the start date of an unused membership package once, to a date from today to today + 7 days; the end date is recomputed from the package duration.
A customer whose profile is Frozen or Inactive cannot create, cancel or pay an online order.

Annual leave uses the yearly quota P-23 minus Approved and Pending annual days. If the remaining quota is smaller than the days requested, the system proposes splitting the request into an Annual part and an Unpaid part; the employee must accept the split, and the balance is re-checked when the request is saved (MSG193, MSG194). One notification is sent for the whole request.

Operational report: From and To dates are required, From ≤ To, with no limit on the range; ranges up to 62 days are charted per day, longer ranges per month. The CSV export contains exactly the displayed report (GBR-33). The Admin report adds audit metrics (CBR-103).
BR: An account that serves only the Customer role and enters a wrong password P-17 (default 5) times in a row is locked for P-18 (default 5) minutes. An account that serves any staff role, including one that also serves the Customer role, is never locked automatically — counter machines are shared, and a wrong lock would stop a whole shift.

When the temporary lock (BR-01) ends, the customer account unlocks and the failure counter resets to 0. A successful sign-in or a password reset through Forgot Password (UC-03) also resets the counter and clears the lock.

Password recovery verifies only through the registered email of the account: the user enters the email (a phone number is not accepted), and the 6-digit code is sent only to that email (GBR-15). Admin-locked or Inactive accounts cannot recover (MSG37).
A password recovery code expires after P-15 (default 15) minutes, and the new password must be saved before that same deadline; the new password follows DBR-02.
The system must always have at least one active Admin account.
The last active Admin account cannot be deleted, locked or demoted, and its employee record cannot be set to Resigned.
Only an Admin can create an Admin account or promote someone to Admin.
The Admin can unlock a temporarily locked customer account early.

When the Admin unlocks an account — locked manually or temporarily after failed sign-ins — a reason of 5–500 characters is required. The unlock resets the failed-attempt counter to 0 and is written to the audit log together with the reason.
The gym's financial parameters are: package prices, VAT, PT commission rate and fees.
The gym has one default opening and closing time for every day (P-19, 05:30–22:00); the Manager declares only the dates that differ — other hours or closed all day (OperatingHourExceptions).
An Inactive employee no longer appears in the list of working staff.

The Manager cannot approve a leave request if, after approval, the staff remaining in any affected shift (GBR-38) would fall below P-13 PTs or P-14 Receptionists (CBR-88, CBR-90). Without a roster, every Working PT and Receptionist counts as on duty in both shifts (CBR-104); other Pending requests are not counted, Approved ones are. Example: with exactly 2 PTs left, no PT may take leave.
A member with no running package and no unused PT session is deleted immediately.
The Receptionist cannot delete on their own a profile that still has a running package or unused PT sessions.
Every deletion of a customer profile requires a reason (5–500 characters).
A profile cannot change between Dependent and self-owned. When a child gets their own phone number, the current package runs out, the old profile is deleted and a new self-owned profile is created.

The Receptionist changes the phone number or email of a customer profile that has an account only when the customer is at the counter and has been checked against the check-in photo; if the profile has no check-in photo yet, the Receptionist checks an identity document and takes the check-in photo on the spot. The change applies to every role of that Person (CBR-110).
When the Receptionist freezes the package of an Active member, the member becomes Frozen.
Only a membership package can be frozen; PT packages (single and couple) cannot.
Freezing a membership package costs P-03 (default 0 = free of charge).
An expired package cannot be frozen. A freeze starts at the earliest tomorrow and its end date cannot be before its start date.
A package that has used up its freeze allowance (P-01, copied into the subscription) cannot be frozen again.
When the freeze period ends, the package reopens automatically (JOB-01) and the member returns to Active; the Receptionist does nothing.

The Receptionist may end a freeze early: the package reopens immediately, the member returns to Active and the end date is extended only by the days actually frozen (DBR-51). The freeze allowance stays used (BR-24, P-01); sessions already closed by JOB-04 are not restored (CBR-68).
A customer who cannot use the gym today (no valid Membership or DayPass, or frozen — CBR-117) cannot check in; a customer holding only a PT package is refused (CBR-58).
Check-in only needs the customer code or phone number (or a name search); no card and no login account are required.
A day pass becomes Used as soon as the customer checks in with it.
A day pass needs no check-in photo and no face comparison.
When checking in a customer holding a package of one month or longer, the Receptionist compares the customer's face with the check-in photo shown on screen and confirms it.
An unused day pass expires at the end of the day (JOB-03).
If a customer with a package of one month or longer has no check-in photo yet (for example after buying online), the Receptionist takes the photo at the first check-in before completing it.
A membership package allows unlimited check-ins within its validity, including several entries on the same day. Only the day pass is limited to a single entry (CBR-36, BR-29).

PT package sessions are generated only on Monday to Friday. The gym itself opens at the weekend like any other day: check-in, day passes, counter sales and single sessions work normally on Saturday and Sunday, and the PT may reschedule a session to a weekend slot (BR-64).
The weekly template and the week tabs of the PT sale screen show only Monday to Friday.

Both members of a couple package must meet CBR-59 and CBR-14 when the order is created; the partner cannot be the holder. A person with only a day pass, or with an expired or frozen membership, cannot join a couple package.
The PT consults the customer in person before the package is sold.
The customer chooses the PT; the PT cannot choose or refuse a customer.

A PT package runs by term: the Receptionist picks the start date (today to today + 30 days, default tomorrow) and the system computes end date = start date + package duration, last day inclusive (GBR-03). The system generates one session for each date in the term that falls on a weekday chosen in the template (CBR-43), unless the date was overridden to "no session" or cannot be scheduled (BR-41). Closed days and days on which the PT has a leave request still get a session, marked amber, for the PT to reschedule (CBR-56, CBR-83). No make-up sessions, no term extension. The number of generated sessions is the number of sessions held.

A date cannot be scheduled when: the time has passed, the customer (or partner) has another session overlapping it, the PT already has a customer then, the slot is held for another order, the PT withdrew that slot, an old slot at that time has a different length, or another slot of the PT overlaps it. The Receptionist may pick another time for that date only (including a slot the PT opened only on that date) or set no session; a date with no workable time gets no session and no make-up.
An order can use at most one voucher.
When a voucher is applied successfully, its used count increases by one.
When an order with a voucher is Cancelled for any reason (CBR-11, CBR-70, CBR-71, CBR-72), one use of the voucher is returned.
When a customer removes a voucher from a Pending order or replaces it, one use of the old voucher is returned; an invalid new code leaves the current discount untouched.
The Receptionist can close a shift only after entering the counted cash; if it differs from the expected cash (DBR-55), a reason is required.
Money from transactions under CBR-72 is refunded to the customer by the Manager outside the system, then confirmed in the system (BR-81).
Only the Receptionist closes a maintenance request (In Progress → Closed), after checking that the item has been repaired, with an acceptance note of 5–500 characters.
Only the Manager approves (Open → In Progress) or rejects (Open → Rejected, reason 5–500 characters) a maintenance request; a request that is no longer Open cannot be decided again.
The number of sessions a PT teaches per day is decided by the PT when publishing slots; the system sets no limit.
A PT may publish slots for any future date, without a limit on weeks or months ahead.
A customer who does not show up has the session deducted: JOB-04 closes it as Missed (CBR-42) and it is never refunded.
For a couple package, deductions are made from the shared quota regardless of who is absent.
Withdrawn — the PT does not mark absences; JOB-04 closes sessions after the session day (CBR-42). P-07 is withdrawn with it.
Withdrawn — there is no Absent button; a no-show becomes Missed / NoCheckIn through JOB-04.
Withdrawn — replaced by CBR-42 and CBR-67 (a couple session is CheckedIn when either member checked in that day).
The PT does not approve or reject individual sessions of a confirmed package schedule.
A PT can edit their own note about a client at any time; saving overwrites the current note.
A PT can delete their own note about a client. The note is hidden permanently (soft delete, GBR-05) and the PT can then write a new note for that client.
A PT can edit a workout or meal plan they created at any time. Edits to a published plan reach the customer only when the PT publishes again; the customer always sees the latest published version.

A PT can delete a workout or meal plan they created. It disappears from the customer's My Plan screen immediately (soft delete, GBR-05), and the PT can then write a new plan of that type for the client.
Withdrawn — the separate "swap on behalf of a customer without an account" option was merged into Reschedule (BR-64); no swap quota is used.

A PT who cannot teach a session, or whose customer asks to move it, agrees with the customer (Zalo / phone) on one of three options — reschedule, transfer to another PT, or cancel with a cash refund — before acting in the system.

Reschedule: the session moves to another Free slot of the same PT, from now up to 14 days ahead and not after the package end date; the target must not be held, must not be on a closed day or in a shift covered by the PT's leave request, and must not overlap another session of the customer or partner. A target day without gym access is allowed but marked (CBR-61). An optional note of up to 500 characters can be added. The session stays Scheduled, keeps its commission, is not deducted and does not use any swap quota; the old slot returns to Free; the move is logged as PtReschedule.

Transfer: the session keeps its date and time and moves to a Free slot of another PT who is Working, whose account is Active and who is free at exactly that time; the receiving PT must not be on leave in that shift. The session stays Scheduled and is not deducted; the PT in charge of the package does not change. The move is logged as PtTransfer and the customer and the receiving PT are notified (CBR-46).

Cancel: the session becomes Cancelled (ByPt); a reason of 5–500 characters and the tick "customer agreed to a cash refund" are mandatory. The slot returns to Free. The system creates no refund transaction.
The money for a session cancelled under BR-66 is returned to the customer in cash by the PT, outside the system.

When a session is transferred, the session value is unchanged and nothing is charged or refunded; the commission is recomputed for the receiving PT: round(session value × receiving PT's commission rate ÷ 100).
A PT who cannot teach a session must handle it in the system (BR-64, BR-65 or BR-66) before the session starts. Violations are dealt with by the Manager outside the system.

Only the PT in charge of the session may reschedule, transfer or cancel it, and only while it is Scheduled and has not started (otherwise MSG91). The Receptionist and Manager do not act on the PT's behalf. Concurrent changes are serialised: a target slot taken meanwhile is refused (MSG103).
A session cancelled under BR-66 is still deducted from the package, because the customer has been repaid in cash.
A customer who cannot use the gym on the chosen date (CBR-117) cannot book a single PT session.
Withdrawn — customers do not swap sessions; P-08 is only stored in the subscription (MaxSwapsSnapshot).
Withdrawn — no swap function exists; the customer contacts the PT (BR-63).
Withdrawn — customers do not cancel sessions (UC-39 withdrawn).

When a transaction becomes Success the order becomes Paid immediately, provided the order is not Cancelled and the amount equals the amount payable exactly; payment and entitlement are written in the same transaction and a repeated gateway call changes nothing.

The Manager confirms in the system that a transaction on the refund list (CBR-72) has been refunded, entering a note of 5–500 characters (bank account or transfer reference). A transaction can be confirmed only once; the confirmation is audited.
A new leave request can only be Annual or Unpaid. Sick remains only on historical requests.
An employee may withdraw their own request while it is Pending; it is removed (GBR-05 exception) and the withdrawal is audited.
An employee cannot have two requests that are not Rejected for the same date and shift.

On the Pending tab the Manager may approve several selected requests at once (1–50, current page only). Each request is re-checked and saved in its own transaction; requests that fail a check stay Pending and their reasons are listed, while the others are approved.
A request whose leave has already started can still be approved, but the Manager must confirm the employee was actually off and give a reason of 5–500 characters; the audit line says "late approval".

Body measurements: one measurement per customer per day — saving again on the same date overwrites it. The date cannot be in the future or before 2000. Weight 20–300 kg and height 100–250 cm are required; body fat 3–70 %, muscle 10–70 % and waist 40–200 cm are optional; note up to 200 characters. The height of the last measurement is pre-filled. Only the customer sees their own measurements; PT measurements at the gym are kept separately.

BMI = weight ÷ height² (m), computed, never stored, and grouped by the Asian scale: < 18.5 underweight, 18.5–22.9 normal, 23–24.9 overweight, ≥ 25 obese. The screen shows five tiles (weight, BMI, body fat, muscle, waist) with the change since the first measurement, a line chart of one chosen metric over real dates, and the history newest first.
The customer may delete one of their own measurements after confirmation; it is removed permanently (GBR-05 exception).

The Exercise Library is a member benefit: a customer may open it when they hold, today, a Membership or PT package whose package has "Unlocks Exercise Library" set and whose term covers today (Active or Frozen; a couple partner counts). Otherwise the screen is locked with the reason — never bought, expired on dd/mm, or starts on dd/mm — and lists the packages that unlock it. A PT can always open it. The check is done on the server; typing the URL does not bypass it.

Exercise Library search: name keyword up to 50 characters, muscle group (8 groups), equipment (12 types), sort by name or "with image first"; 12 exercises per page; an unknown value is ignored and the page number is clamped to the valid range. Names stay in English; groups, muscles and equipment are shown in Vietnamese.

Exercise data come from the public wger API (API-05) and are cached. The cache is refreshed when it is empty or older than 1 day, replacing all rows in one transaction. If wger fails, the old data stay with a notice of the last update and the next attempt is made 5 minutes later; if there is no data at all, an error with a reload action is shown (MSG306). An exercise without a wger image gets an illustration chosen by exercise name or muscle group, labelled as an illustration, without repeating an image on the same page. The wger source and licence (CC BY-SA 4.0) are credited on the page.

PT sale hold: "Hold schedule" creates a Pending counter order and puts every chosen slot on Held for 15 minutes (a fixed value), creating Held slots where the PT had none; other Receptionists and the PT see them as held. Payment is accepted only while the hold is valid. "Release hold" (after confirmation) or expiry cancels the order, deletes the slots created by the hold and returns the others to Free; expired holds are released the next time the PT sale screen is used. No voucher can be applied (CBR-76).

PT slot publishing: new slots are drafts until the PT presses Publish; publishing sends all drafts and removals in one transaction and saves all or nothing. Each new slot must start on a 15-minute mark in the future, lie fully within the opening hours of that date (not a closed day), have length P-06, not overlap a shift covered by the PT's Pending or Approved leave, and not overlap another draft or a published slot. A draft at the start time of a withdrawn slot reopens that slot if the lengths are equal. Publishing with no change is refused (MSG320); if P-06 changed since the page was opened, the PT must reload (MSG321).

The PT can withdraw only their own Free slots that have not started, have no Scheduled session and are not held; withdrawal sets them to Withdrawn (never deleted). Helpers only prepare drafts: "Remove all free slots" of the week, "Copy week to next week" (slots that cannot be added are skipped and counted) and a date picker.

When a PT-sale date uses a time the PT has not opened on that date, the screen marks it "PT not opened"; the hold is refused until the Receptionist ticks "Confirmed with PT". The system then creates that slot as Held.

When a PT sale is paid: the order becomes Paid with a Success transaction (cash, or transfer with optional reference up to 50 characters), the subscription is created with session value = round(price ÷ number of sessions) and commission = round(session value × PT commission rate ÷ 100) per session, and the holder, the partner and the PT receive a bell notification.

My Bookings (view only): lists the customer's PT packages (in progress / ended) and single sessions; for the chosen package it shows the next session, progress, the weekly template (the start time used by at least half of that weekday's sessions, ties → earliest; other sessions are listed as "different time" with the move reason), the session strip and the "watch" list (upcoming warnings, absences, cancellations). It shows at most one call to action, by priority: buy a membership (an upcoming session without gym access) > buy a PT package at the counter (≥ 3 single sessions in 30 days) > rejoin at the counter (package ended) > renew at the counter (≤ 3 sessions or ≤ 14 days left).

My PT Sessions (view only): week timetable in three bands by start time — morning (before 13:00), afternoon (13:00–17:59), evening (from 18:00) — or month calendar. Each session shows one of: today, upcoming, needs attention (no gym access, frozen or closed day), result pending (ended, waiting for JOB-04), checked in, missed (with reason), cancelled (with reason). The detail shows the PT, package, status and reason, a Zalo link, copy phone and an "add to Google Calendar" link. Customers cannot cancel or move sessions.

PT schedule week view: each slot is shown as free, held (order awaiting payment), locked (leave pending / approved) or booked; a booked session shows upcoming → in progress → result pending, or its result. A slot can be added from the opening time (rounded up to 15 minutes; today only after the current time) until closing time minus P-06 (rounded down); a closed day accepts no new slot. The grid shows the 13:00 shift divider.

PT dashboard: today's schedule for 7 days (today to today + 6), the "needs attention" list for the next 14 days (sessions without gym access, inside a freeze period or on a closed day — with a link to handle the session), the assigned packages with the customer's phone and Zalo link, the monthly result and commission (CheckedIn, Missed by reason, Cancelled; commission from stored amounts) and the weather forecast (API-04).

Customer dashboard: shows the profile, whether the customer can use the gym today (CBR-117), packages in use or not started, the next 5 PT sessions, up to five warning banners (red: profile Expired, a session on a day without gym access; amber: profile Frozen with the freeze period, membership ending within 7 days unless a chained package exists, a Pending online order awaiting payment), the monthly attendance streak and the 5 latest notifications. It only reads statuses; it never changes them.

Notification bell: shows the 10 latest notifications of the signed-in account with read / unread state; the user can mark one or all as read. Notifications created by the system have no sender (GBR-15).

Facilities are managed as groups and items: a facility group has a name (3–100 characters), category, location, unit label (up to 15 characters), image and visibility; each physical equipment item has a code unique in the whole system (2–20 characters, e.g. TM-001), a label unique within its group (1–50 characters, e.g. "12 kg"), a placement note (up to 100 characters) and a status Available, UnderMaintenance or Retired. Quantities are computed, never typed: total = items not Retired; available = Available items without an Open or In Progress request; under maintenance = items UnderMaintenance or with such a request.

Reporting broken equipment is a two-step flow: (1) choose the facility group and one or more of its items — items that are Retired, UnderMaintenance or already have an Open or In Progress request cannot be selected, so an item has at most one open request; (2) enter priority (default Normal), incident type, description (10–500 characters), optional affected-items note (up to 100 characters), whether a warning tag was placed, and optional images. One request (BT-nnnn) is created per item, all in one transaction — if any item is missing or Retired nothing is saved — and every Manager receives one bell notification.

When deciding a maintenance request the Manager sees the item's last closed request and the availability of its group, may add a note of up to 500 characters and chooses "Set item to Under maintenance" (CBR-101). The reporting Receptionist is notified of the approval or rejection; the approving Manager is notified when the request is closed.

Package catalogue: name 3–50 characters and unique among packages on sale; price 10,000–500,000,000 VND in multiples of 1,000; description up to 255 characters; benefits (DBR-15); "Unlocks Exercise Library". A membership lasts one of the durations in P-04 (default 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36 months), a day pass exactly 1 day, a PT package one of the durations in P-21 (default 1, 3, 6, 12 months) with 1–255 estimated sessions. Single-session packages can be edited but not created. "Stop selling" never affects sold packages (CBR-97); selling again requires a unique name and an allowed duration. Saves use a row-version check (MSG22) and are audited.

Manager leave list: opens on the Pending tab; Pending, Approved and Rejected list requests, All groups requests by employee. Pending requests are ordered with leave starting today or tomorrow first, then by submission time; decided requests by decision time, newest first. Filters: employee name or code, position, leave type and submission date range (empty by default). Clicking a row opens the detail; Approve and Reject (with reason) are also available on the row.

Business event times (paid, cancelled, checked in, reviewed, closed, read…) are written when the event happens and never edited.
A phone number must follow the Vietnamese format: 10 digits, starting with 0, with a valid 3-digit carrier prefix (P-16).
An email must follow the format name@domain and be at most 100 characters.

A day pass lasts exactly 1 day. A membership package and a PT package last a whole number of months chosen from the duration lists configured by the Manager — P-04 (default 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36 months) and P-21 (default 1, 3, 6, 12 months); the package catalogue offers only these values. The database accepts 1–36 months for a membership package and 1–12 months for a PT package. End dates are computed by calendar month (GBR-03), never as 30 days.
A PT slot lasts P-06 minutes (default 90) when it is published; one slot on a PT's calendar holds one session. A slot keeps the length it was published with even if P-06 changes later.
There are two kinds of PT package: single (PTSingle) and couple (PTCouple); SingleSession is a one-session package.

A phone number is stored on Person and must not duplicate any other active Person, customer or staff alike. A Person is active while at least one of its roles (customer profile or employee record) is not Inactive. Every Person has a phone number except a Dependent profile (DBR-24), because the phone number is what the Receptionist and the Admin use to find an existing Person (CBR-19, CBR-114).

An email is stored on Person and must not duplicate any other active Person (DBR-22). It is mandatory for every Person who has a login account and for every Self customer profile (CBR-18); it is not used for a Dependent profile (DBR-26). A rejected duplicate only says the email is already in use, never whose it is.
UC-04, UC-05, UC-07, UC-16, UC-20, UC-IDENT

A Dependent customer profile has no phone of its own on Person; it is reached through the guardian phone numbers recorded on the profile, which several dependants may share — siblings may use the same guardian number — as long as the guardian's full name and relationship are recorded.
A Dependent profile records the guardian's full name (2–50 characters), relationship (up to 30 characters) and up to two guardian phone numbers, so a child can be reached through either parent.
A Dependent profile has no email and no account.
A staff member and a customer who are the same individual share one Person record, so they have one phone number and one email; there is never a separate staff phone or email list.

When a role becomes Inactive (customer profile deleted, employee resigned) while the Person still has another role that is not Inactive, the Person keeps its phone number and email. When every role of the Person is Inactive, the phone number and email are released immediately and the person can get a new profile without waiting (CBR-23).
One Person, several roles, one account: the same individual working as staff and training as a customer keeps one Person, one phone number, one email and one login account (DBR-65).
A walk-in customer still needs a profile: Self profiles need full name, date of birth, phone number and email (CBR-118); Dependent profiles need the guardian fields.
A slot of a PT is assigned to one customer only, or to one pair of customers for a couple package; it has at most one Scheduled session.
Slots of a PT must not overlap (checked when publishing, holding and moving sessions); apart from that the PT decides whether slots are back-to-back or spaced out.
A customer profile has exactly five states: New, Active, Frozen, Expired, Inactive.
Inactive is a final state; an Inactive profile never returns to any other state.

A PT slot has four states: Free, Held, Booked, Withdrawn. A slot becomes Held when an order reserves it: an online single-session order until its payment deadline (P-09), or a PT-sale hold for 15 minutes (HoldExpiresAt, BR-93). When the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked. When the order is cancelled, released or expires, the slot returns to Free (a slot created only for that hold is deleted). When a session is moved or cancelled by the PT, its old slot returns to Free. A Free slot that the PT removes becomes Withdrawn and is kept; publishing the same start time again reopens it (BR-94, BR-95).

A session has four states: Scheduled, CheckedIn, Missed, Cancelled. Missed always has a reason (NoCheckIn, NoMembership, MembershipFrozen); Cancelled always has a type (ByPt, ByCustomer — historical, GymClosed, PackageExpired).
A session in a final state (CheckedIn, Missed, Cancelled) cannot be changed by anyone. Only JOB-04 moves a session from Scheduled to CheckedIn or Missed.
An order has three states: Pending, Paid, Cancelled. There is no refunded state — refunds are paid outside the system and only confirmed on the transaction (BR-81).
UC-20, UC-21, UC-22, UC-24, UC-25, UC-26, UC-PAY
An order moves only along Pending → Paid, Pending → Cancelled, and Paid → Cancelled (only under CBR-11). Cancelled is final.
Every payment attempt for an order is recorded as a transaction with four states: Pending, Success, Failed, Expired. One order may have several transactions.
UC-20, UC-21, UC-22, UC-24, UC-26, UC-PAY
An order has at most one Success transaction and at most one Pending transaction at any time. A Paid order gets no further transactions.

A cancelled order records its cancellation type: payment deadline passed (CBR-70), replaced by a new order (CBR-71), invalid payment (CBR-72) or cancelled by the Receptionist (CBR-11, and PT-sale holds released or expired — BR-93, with the reason text).
A leave request has three states: Pending, Approved, Rejected. A Pending request withdrawn by its owner is removed (BR-83).
A maintenance request has four states: Open, In Progress, Rejected, Closed.

A maintenance request moves only along Open → In Progress → Closed, or Open → Rejected; no step is skipped. In Progress records the reviewer, review time, the "set under maintenance" choice and an optional Manager note; Rejected records a reason of at least 5 characters; Closed records the closing Receptionist, time and an acceptance note of 5–500 characters.

A customer whose state is Active, Frozen or Expired is a member (isMember = TRUE), including someone who has only ever bought a day pass. Once a member, always a member; whether the person can currently use the gym is expressed by canUseService.

canUseService on a date = the customer can use the gym on that date as defined in CBR-117 (a Membership or DayPass covering the date, not frozen). A PT package or remaining PT sessions never make it TRUE (CBR-58).
A profile without its own phone number, using a guardian's number, is a Dependent profile.
When an order is created, the current package name, description, benefits, price and VAT rate are copied into the order; later catalogue changes never affect it (CBR-09).
New end date = old end date + the number of days actually frozen.

A day pass starts and ends on the day it is paid. A new membership package starts the day after the current membership ends if it has not expired; otherwise today, or a date chosen up to 7 days ahead at the counter, and an unused online package may be moved once within 7 days (CBR-119). End date = start date + package duration (DBR-19, GBR-03).

PT packages are sold by term, not by number of sessions. The session count of an order is the number of sessions held at sale (BR-40) and is fixed when the order is Paid. Catalogues and public pages show only the estimated session count of the package.
A couple PT package shares one quota between both members.
Expected cash at shift close = the sum of Success cash transactions recorded in that shift for orders that are not Cancelled.
Revenue = the sum of Success transactions of orders that are not Cancelled. Refunds made outside the system are not deducted.

The order detail shows the tax breakdown: Amount payable = package price at purchase − discount; VAT amount = Amount payable × VAT% ÷ (100 + VAT%), rounded to the dong and stored on the order at creation; Pre-tax amount = Amount payable − VAT amount.
UC-20, UC-21, UC-24, UC-26, UC-46, UC-PAY
PT commission of a session = round(session value × commission rate of the PT teaching it ÷ 100), stored on the session when it is created and recomputed only on a transfer (BR-68).
Session value = round(amount paid for the order ÷ number of sessions generated for that order) (BR-40); PT packages have no discount (CBR-76).

Remaining staff of a shift (per role, PT / Receptionist) = Working employees of that role − those with Approved leave overlapping the shift. Without a roster, every Working employee counts as on duty in both shifts (CBR-104).

At sale the subscription stores the freeze allowance (P-01, membership only), the swap allowance MaxSwapsSnapshot = P-08 × package months (PT packages) and, for PT packages, the PT in charge and the fixed start time (the most frequent session time).
At most one active plan per (PT, customer, plan type — workout or meal). A deleted plan does not count, so a new one may be written after deletion.
At most one record per (employee, work date, shift type); check-out time must be later than check-in time. Modelled only — staff timekeeping is out of scope for this release.

Avatar: JPG or PNG, max 5 MB, from 200 × 200 to 2000 × 2000 px; a non-square image is cropped to the centre and stored at 256 × 256 px. A Person has at most one customer profile that is not Inactive, at most one employee record with status Working, and at most one login Account that serves every non-Inactive role; an Inactive role does not block creating a new role of the same kind (CBR-114).
Feedback content is 10–1000 characters. A feedback may rate one PT with 1–5 stars for a month (rating month = first day of that month); without a PT there is no rating.
A customer has at most one rating per PT per month. Rating the same PT again in the same month overwrites the stars and content and makes the feedback unread again (CBR-107).
Monthly average of a PT = total stars ÷ number of customers who rated that PT in the month, truncated to two decimals (4.999 shows 4.99); shown to the PT with a short encouragement text.
The average is shown only when at least P-22 (default 3) customers rated the PT that month; otherwise the PT sees "no rating yet" or "not enough ratings yet".
At most one measurement per customer per date (BR-87); weight 20–300 kg, height 100–250 cm, body fat 3–70 %, muscle 10–70 %, waist 40–200 cm, one decimal; BMI is derived, not stored (BR-88).

ItemCode is unique in the whole system; ItemLabel is unique within its facility group; status Available, UnderMaintenance or Retired (Retired is final).

NFR: Java 17; Jakarta Servlet 6.0 / JSP with JSTL 3.0 (MVC: Servlet – Service – DAO); Apache Tomcat 10.1; Microsoft SQL Server with mssql-jdbc 13.4; jBCrypt 0.4 for password hashing; Gson 2.11 for JSON; Angus Mail 2.0 (SMTP) for email; Apache POI 5.3 for Excel export; JUnit 5 and Mockito 5 for unit tests; Maven build; Git / GitHub for source control. Background jobs run on the JDK scheduler inside the application (no extra library).

VNPay payment gateway (sandbox) for online payment (API-01, API-02); an SMTP mailbox for verification codes, temporary passwords and alerts (API-03); Open-Meteo for the PT dashboard weather (API-04); wger.de public exercise API for the Exercise Library (API-05). When an external service is unavailable the related feature shows an error message (or its last cached data) and the rest of the system keeps working.

The interface is in Vietnamese; dates dd/mm/yyyy, times 24-hour, money in VND with thousand separators (GBR-01, GBR-02, GBR-29). Every error is a message from section System Messages, shown next to the field it concerns or as a toast (GBR-17). Each main screen has an (i) hint box for its explanations instead of a subtitle line (GBR-36). Texts shown to users never contain rule codes (GBR-37). Statuses always have a text label besides their colour (GBR-28).

The web application is used on current versions of Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Every main screen is usable at 390 px (phone), 768 / 1024 px (tablet) and 1440 px (desktop) without horizontal page scrolling (GBR-35); calendars switch to a one-day or list view on narrow screens. Light and dark themes keep readable contrast.

Passwords and temporary passwords are stored only as BCrypt hashes and are never shown or logged (DBR-02). Every page except the public pages, Sign In, Register and Forgot Password requires sign-in, and every request is checked against the role the user is working in (GBR-10, GBR-13). Every POST made while signed in carries a CSRF token that is checked on the server (MSG214); the only POSTs without it are Sign In, Register, Forgot Password and the VNPay IPN, which is verified by its signature instead. A sign-in session expires after 2 hours without activity (GBR-31); a password change or reset signs out the other sessions (CBR-93). Database access uses parameterised queries only; sort and filter values are taken from fixed lists. All output is HTML-escaped. Uploaded images are JPG or PNG up to 5 MB and 2000 px.

No business record is physically deleted except the cases listed in GBR-05. A deleted customer profile keeps its row as Inactive together with its orders, transactions, subscriptions, check-ins and sessions, so revenue and tax records stay complete. Every multi-step change (sale, payment, session handling, publishing slots, leave decision, maintenance decision) runs in one database transaction with its audit line (GBR-07, GBR-08); concurrent changes are resolved by locks and conditional updates (GBR-13, GBR-32).

Under normal use at one gym, a screen opens and a save completes within a few seconds. Filtering, counting, sorting and paging are done in SQL, never by loading whole tables; page sizes per screen follow GBR-18.

The system serves one gym in one time zone (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh). There is no SMS, no mobile app, no e-invoice and no in-system refund; these are handled outside the system (GBR-15, GBR-16). Daily background jobs run at 00:05 and minute jobs run every minute (GBR-14).

Each background job processes records one by one in separate transactions, so one failing record does not stop the others. A daily job that hits a database error is retried every 5 minutes; jobs are idempotent (running twice changes nothing more, e.g. JOB-08 never sends the same reminder twice).

Every action can be done with the keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Escape closes dialogs and hint boxes and returns focus); icons have text alternatives; dialogs trap focus; on a small screen icon-only buttons keep their accessible names.
UC: Authenticate with an email address or phone number plus a password; either identifies exactly one account. If the account serves more than one role that is not Inactive, the user chooses the working role on Select Role; the role can be switched later without signing in again. Customer-only accounts are locked temporarily after P-17 wrong passwords (BR-01). Customers whose account was created at the counter sign in with the temporary password received by email (CBR-31); the Sign In screen explains this in a hint box.
End the current session and securely sign out.

Reset a forgotten password in three steps — enter the registered email, enter the 6-digit code (valid P-15 minutes), set a new password before the code deadline. The reset clears a temporary lock and signs out every session (CBR-93). Also used by customers who lost their counter temporary password.

One Account Settings screen for all five roles. Change avatar (upload or remove), email and phone number (each with a 6-digit verification code — CBR-110) and password (current password required, new password different, other sessions signed out). Personnel data is read-only (CBR-108); customers also see a read-only Dependent profiles tab (CBR-111).
Self-register as a new customer directly on the website; phone/email uniqueness is validated against existing records.

A Pending request can be withdrawn (BR-83).

Create, look up and update customer profiles at the counter, including walk-in and dependent profiles, and capture the check-in photo used to verify entry. Approve/reject pending deletion requests for members with an active package/unused quota, reviewing the reason submitted by Receptionist.

Pause an active membership package (never a PT package or an expired package) for a fee of P-03 (default free), within the freeze count and length limits (P-01, P-02), starting tomorrow at the earliest. A freeze is never blocked by PT sessions: before saving, the system lists the Scheduled sessions inside the freeze period; they stay Scheduled with a warning and JOB-04 closes them after each session day (CBR-62). The package resumes automatically at the end of the freeze (JOB-01); the Receptionist may also end it early, and the end date moves out only by the days actually frozen (DBR-51). A Receptionist cannot freeze their own package (CBR-115).

Verify the face against the check-in photo (take it if missing — BR-33) and record the check-in.
